Your are developing an employee data set of a fictional company to be used for people analytics analysis. I will provide you with a csv file that contains the variables. Below is a desription of the variables that may be confusing, the remaining I assume you will understand. I will also provide you with how I would like to see the distribution of the variable. This is a world wide company servicing multiple regions. They are a technology company that provides a range of services, include but not limited to platform engineering, IT Project management, development, operations, Analysis and the so forth. Fill in the gaps. I want 30 years of data starting in 2002. Start with 300 employees. Gender is 50 - 50 through out the years, with a standard diviation of 8. Employees should be between 20 years of age and 72 years. Average age is 42 with a standard deviation of 7.  There is a 5% growth rate with standard deviation of 4. Attrition rate is 6% with a standard deviation of 2.5. The retiremenet rate starts at 2% in year five and peaks at 15% in year 15, then stabalizes at 5%. The retirement eligible age is 65, early retiremet is acceptable at 60 years of age. 


- business area text:  equivalent to a department. create 9 departments, one top level and tbe rest under that.
- business area key:  unique key of the business area or department.
- region key: identifier for the regions the company services
- region text: the regions the company services. Create 6 world wide regions
- current pay period: the pay period, the first 4 numbers represent the year and the last two are the pay period, of which there is 26
- date accession: is the employee's start date
- date retirement early out: date the employee is eleigibel to take early retirement
- date retirement eligible: date the employee is eligible to retire
-  email address work: employee's email address, use 'first name.lastname' pattern and change to end in '@paverse.ai'
-  grade: this is the level of the employee from 1 - 15, 1 being the lowest and 15 the highest.
- organization title: these are divisions or groups under the departments. randomly create between 2 and 5 under each business area with the exception of the top level which is just one.
- position class code key: unique identifier for position class code 
- postion class code text: this is the positon type. make sure they represent the orgainzation you created and align with occupational series. the same position can be in different busniess areas and/or organizations. 
- supervisory status text: is the employee a supervisor or not, 20% of the worlforce are supervisors with a standard deviation of 3.
- time in grade: time the employee has been in there current grade
- emp_id: unique identifier of the employee, cannot repeat.
- year: calendar year of the employee
- date effective: the date the gain of loss was effective
- type of gain: types of gains are new hire, term hire, reassignment, intern. Reassignment means it was an internal move. 15% term hire, 12% reassignment, 5% interns the rest new hires, per year.
- type of loss: Resign, Terminated, retired, reassignment. I gave you the retirement rate alredy. termination is 3% reassignment matches gains, and the rest resign. 

Do your best to keep the logic sound, you are clear to increase devation from these numbers in order to make the math work
